title: Attach supplied finite free cone cycles detected by functors
statement: Let $R$ and $B_j$ for $j\in\operatorname{Fin}(r)$ be commutative rings in the same universe. Let $L_j:\operatorname{Mod}(R)\to\operatorname{Mod}(B_j)$ be additive functors preserving epimorphisms. Let $f:F\to C$ be a chain map of integer-indexed cochain complexes of $R$-modules (degree-one differentials square to zero), and $n,b\in\mathbb Z$ satisfy $n\le b+1$. Assume $F^i=0$ for $i<n$ and $i>b$, and its terms are finite free. Put $D=\operatorname{Cone}(f)$, with $D^i=F^{i+1}\oplus C^i$ and differential $(-d_F,f+d_C)$. Assume $L_j(H^i(D))=0$ for $i\ge n$. Let $P$ be a finite free $R$-module and $q:P\to Z^{n-1}(D)$ a map to the kernel of the outgoing cone differential, such that every $L_j(\pi\circ q)$ is epic, where $\pi\circ q$ denotes the source-to-target composite $P\to Z^{n-1}(D)\to H^{n-1}(D)$. There are a complex $G$, a map $g:G\to C$, and $\tau:F\to G$ such that $G$ is zero outside $[n-1,b]$, all terms of $G$ are finite free, $L_j(H^i(\operatorname{Cone}(g)))=0$ for $i\ge n-1$, $g\tau=f$, and every $\tau^i$ for $i\ge n$ is invertible. No exactness or faithfulness of the detecting functors and no global epimorphism of $\pi\circ q$ are assumed.

source.place: Tag 08EE, proof of lemma-lift-pseudo-coherent, cone-cycle attachment after the finite family is supplied; https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08EE

proof.text: Project the supplied cone cycles to obtain a:P to F^n and c:P to C^(n-1) with a d_F=0 and a f+c d_C=0. Let A be the single complex P in degree n, k:A to F induced by a, and let the degree-minus-one cochain -c have coboundary k f. Construct G=Cone(k), g=desc(k,-c,f), and tau=inr(k). The cone identities give tau g=f. The termwise biproducts of the single complex and F give the support and finite free bounds. In retained degrees the single term is zero, making tau invertible. This is the construction of the existing proved cone-cycle attachment, with the generator and vanishing hypotheses only used after functor application.

Construct t:Cone(f) to Cone(g) using tau and the identity on C. Its components in degrees at least n-1 are invertible, so homologyMap(t,i) is epic there. The images of the supplied cycles under t are boundaries of minus the new P-term, so q homologyProjection homologyMap(t,n-1)=0. Apply L_j: both L_j(q homologyProjection) and L_j(homologyMap(t,n-1)) are epic and their composite is zero. Thus the latter is zero and epic, making its target zero. In higher degrees L_j(homologyMap(t,i)) is epic with zero source by the hypothesis, making its target zero.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_finiteFree_cone_cycle_attachment_functors (R : Type u) [CommRing R]
    (r : ℕ) (B : Fin r → Type u) [∀ j, CommRing (B j)]
    (L : ∀ j, ModuleCat.{u} R ⥤ ModuleCat.{u} (B j))
    [∀ j, (L j).Additive] [∀ j, (L j).PreservesEpimorphisms]
    (C F : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} R) ℤ) (f : F ⟶ C) (b n : ℤ)
    (hn : n ≤ b + 1) (hlow : F.IsStrictlyGE n) (hupp : F.IsStrictlyLE b)
    (hfree : ∀ i : ℤ, Module.Free R (F.X i) ∧ Module.Finite R (F.X i))
    (hvan : ∀ j : Fin r, ∀ i : ℤ, n ≤ i →
      IsZero ((L j).obj ((CochainComplex.mappingCone f).homology i)))
    (P : ModuleCat.{u} R) [Module.Free R P] [Module.Finite R P]
    (q : P ⟶ (CochainComplex.mappingCone f).cycles (n - 1))
    (hq : ∀ j : Fin r,
      Epi ((L j).map (q ≫ (CochainComplex.mappingCone f).homologyπ (n - 1)))) :
    ∃ (G : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} R) ℤ) (g : G ⟶ C) (j : F ⟶ G),
      G.IsStrictlyGE (n - 1) ∧ G.IsStrictlyLE b ∧
      (∀ i : ℤ, Module.Free R (G.X i) ∧ Module.Finite R (G.X i)) ∧
      (∀ j : Fin r, ∀ i : ℤ, n - 1 ≤ i →
        IsZero ((L j).obj ((CochainComplex.mappingCone g).homology i))) ∧
      j ≫ g = f ∧ (∀ i : ℤ, n ≤ i → IsIso (j.f i))
